paragraphs: Interpolation estimates a function between locations where its values are known. Traditional numerical approaches can enforce exact agreement at those locations, whereas neural interpolation methods may leave errors there. This paper treats those errors as useful observations: they reveal what the current estimate still needs to capture.

The proposed Hierarchical INTerpolation Network, or HINT, arranges lightweight interpolation blocks in sequence. The first block predicts the main part of the function. Later blocks use errors remaining at observed points to predict additional corrections. Adding the main prediction and these corrections produces the final estimate, so each stage has a more specific residual problem to solve.

HINT also restricts how observed and target points interact at successive stages. This design assumes that finer residual corrections require attention to a more local set of observations. Experiments report substantially better interpolation accuracy than existing algorithms across varied datasets. These findings support residual refinement as a practical design strategy, without establishing that the final neural interpolant always has zero error at observed points.
neurips-2023-accurate-interpolation-for-.tldr: HINT improves neural interpolation by repeatedly predicting and adding corrections guided by errors at observed points.

paragraphs: Point clouds describe objects through collections of points, but useful information can also lie in their overall structure. Persistent homology extracts global topological features by examining an increasing sequence of spaces called a filtration. The choice of this sequence strongly affects how useful the resulting features are for a learning task.

The paper proposes learning the filtration with a neural network so that it can adapt to the data and prediction objective. It also develops an architecture designed to make the resulting persistent homology invariant to isometries: transformations that preserve distances. This connects task-specific feature learning with a requirement that equivalent geometric arrangements receive consistent topological descriptions.

A theoretical result concerning finite-dimensional approximations of filtration functions provides justification for the architecture. Experiments on several classification tasks demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The contribution is therefore both a method for adapting topological feature extraction and a principled way to retain geometric invariance while doing so, rather than relying on a fixed filtration choice across tasks.
neurips-2023-adaptive-topological-featur.tldr: The paper learns task-adaptive filtrations for point-cloud topology while preserving invariance to distance-preserving transformations.

paragraphs: Models of neural populations often learn compact representations by reconstructing the same activity they receive as input. That objective does not require predicting how activity develops over time. This paper instead studies forecasting, which could encourage representations to capture temporal causality constraints, while acknowledging the difficulty posed by limited recordings and trials.

AMAG introduces a prior based on pairwise interactions among neural units within a multivariate dynamical system. Its graph neural network combines additive and multiplicative message passing, drawing an analogy to interactions in neuronal systems. The model adaptively learns relationships among units and uses them to estimate future activity, making interaction modeling part of the forecasting process.

The authors evaluate AMAG on synthetic data and multiple forms of neural recordings from four rhesus macaques, including penetrating-electrode field potentials and surface micro-electrocorticography. They report advantages over methods without graph neural networks, recovery of ground-truth spatial interactions, and prediction of future population dynamics. These results support the interaction-based forecasting approach; the motivation concerning causality remains a potential benefit of the training task.
neurips-2023-amag-additive-multiplicativ.tldr: AMAG learns additive and multiplicative interactions among neural units to improve forecasts of neural population activity.

paragraphs: This paper studies task selection when both rewards and completion times are initially unknown. A decision maker repeatedly starts tasks while ensuring that the currently running set satisfies a combinatorial constraint. Each task reveals its reward and processing time only after completion, so decisions must account for ongoing work as well as incomplete information.

The proposed algorithm combines upper confidence bounds with updates organized into phases. Upper confidence bounds support exploration of uncertain choices, while the phased approach structures how estimates are revised. The setting extends stochastic combinatorial semi-bandits and budget-constrained bandits by explicitly incorporating the time tasks spend processing.

The authors prove two bounds on regret, the accumulated performance shortfall relative to an optimal choice. One grows as O(MN log(T)/Δ), while a gap-free bound grows as Õ(√MNT). Here N counts tasks, M limits simultaneous tasks, T is the horizon, and Δ measures the expected per-round reward gap between optimal and best suboptimal task sets. These bounds nearly match lower bounds, indicating strong theoretical performance for this setting.
neurips-2023-bandit-task-assignment-with.tldr: A confidence-based algorithm learns which tasks to run when rewards and processing times are unknown, with nearly matching regret upper and lower bounds.

paragraphs: Maximum likelihood estimation trains language models to explain observed text through a probability distribution. This paper argues that estimating the full distribution is not always necessary or optimal, particularly for closed-ended tasks such as translation, where the aim is to produce a highly appropriate answer rather than represent every plausible output equally well.

The authors introduce training objectives built from convex functions that concentrate learning on highly probable outputs. Their theoretical analysis shows that these functions can sharpen the optimal predicted distribution. This provides a connection between the mathematical form of the loss and the model's emphasis on its strongest candidate responses.

Experiments across generation tasks and model types report benefits from this approach. For autoregressive models, it narrows the gap between greedy decoding and beam search. For non-autoregressive models, the largest reported improvement exceeds nine BLEU points. The authors also report improved generation by large language models. Together, these findings support changing the training objective to better match output selection, especially when a task rewards a focused response.
neurips-2023-beyond-mle-convex-learning-.tldr: Convex training objectives sharpen text models' predicted distributions and improve generation by emphasizing highly probable outputs.

paragraphs: Transformers face a memory bottleneck when processing long sequences. Both self-attention and the large feedforward network contribute to this demand, restricting training on inputs that contain extensive context or long-term dependencies. This paper addresses the execution of these computations so that longer sequences can fit within memory.

Blockwise Parallel Transformer, or BPT, combines blockwise self-attention computation with feedforward network fusion. The approach coordinates these parts of the model to reduce their memory costs. Its contribution therefore concerns how Transformer computations are organized, with the goal of making longer training inputs practical while retaining memory efficiency.

The authors report support for training sequences 32 times longer than vanilla Transformers and up to four times longer than earlier memory-efficient methods. Experiments on language modeling and reinforcement learning show reduced memory requirements alongside improved performance. These findings connect an implementation-level change to the ability to train with more context. The reported sequence-length comparisons describe the demonstrated gains; they do not establish an identical increase for every model or workload.
neurips-2023-blockwise-parallel-transfor.tldr: BPT reduces Transformer memory use through blockwise attention and feedforward fusion, enabling substantially longer training sequences.

paragraphs: Separating individual objects in a 3D scene is difficult partly because large annotated 3D datasets are scarce. Contrastive Lift draws on pretrained 2D instance-segmentation models instead. The goal is to turn object segments found in individual images into a coherent account of the separate objects occupying a scene.

The method lifts those 2D segments into 3D and combines them through a neural field representation. This representation encourages agreement across different views. A slow-fast clustering objective provides the central mechanism for grouping the lifted information and is designed to scale to scenes containing many objects. The approach requires neither a preset upper bound on object count nor object tracking across frames.

To examine this scalability, the authors introduce Messy Rooms, a semi-realistic dataset with as many as 500 objects in a scene. They report state-of-the-art improvements on challenging scenes from ScanNet, Hypersim, Replica, and Messy Rooms. The results support using consistent fusion of existing 2D predictions to address 3D instance segmentation, including scenes with substantial object counts.
neurips-2023-contrastive-lift-3d-object-.tldr: Contrastive Lift fuses pretrained 2D object segments into consistent 3D instances without requiring object tracking or a fixed object-count limit.

paragraphs: Salient object detection identifies elements that stand out in a scene. Existing work has used either depth information alongside color images or temporal information from video to improve detection in complex scenes. Studying both together has been constrained by the availability of suitable data, motivating this paper's dataset and benchmark.

The authors introduce DViSal, a collection of 237 diverse videos containing both color and depth information. Its annotations include object-level and instance-level markings, bounding boxes, and scribbles. These different annotation forms make the collection relevant to a range of research directions rather than only one narrowly specified prediction format.

The paper also benchmarks multiple salient-object detection models and reports evidence that multimodal video input benefits the task. This establishes a shared experimental resource for investigating how depth and temporal cues can work together. The publicly accessible dataset and benchmark results are central contributions: they provide both examples to study and reference evaluations for subsequent work in RGB-D video salient object detection.
neurips-2023-dvsod-rgb-d-video-salient-o.tldr: DViSal supplies annotated color-and-depth videos and benchmarks to support salient object detection using depth and temporal information together.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks differ in their ability to distinguish graph structures. Standard message-passing networks are limited by the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Lehman test. Higher-order versions offer more expressive power, but require substantial storage and traditionally provide a rigid design choice centered on the order k.

The paper introduces two extensions. The first, (k, t)-FWL, creates an expressiveness hierarchy reaching graph isomorphism while keeping space complexity at O(n^k) for any fixed k of at least two. The second, k-FWL+, allows equivariant neighbor sets, expanding which relationships the procedure can consider. Together they form a framework that can reproduce most existing models with matching expressiveness. The fixed-space result concerns storage, rather than a claim that all such computations are cheap.

A concrete instance, Neighborhood²-FWL, is proved at least as powerful as 3-WL while requiring O(n²) space and encoding many substructures. Its neural version, N²-GNN, reports record results of 0.059 on ZINC-Subset and 71.8% on BREC. These results connect the broader theoretical design space to an empirically effective architecture.
neurips-2023-extending-the-design-space-.tldr: Extensions of Folklore Weisfeiler-Lehman enable more flexible graph models, including a quadratic-space model with at least 3-WL expressiveness.

paragraphs: Graph contrastive learning often constructs altered graph views and labels pairs as positive or negative. This creates two difficulties: deciding whether an alteration preserves the underlying label and deciding how similar two representations should become. GALOPA proposes a self-supervised alternative that avoids requiring this positive-versus-negative distinction.

Its objective aligns optimal transport plans between the input graphs and their learned node representations. A transport plan describes matching probabilities, so alignment preserves information about which elements correspond across graphs. The approach aims to retain both internal graph structure and relationships between graphs. The paper also identifies distance-preserving embeddings as a consequence of its objective.

Experiments find that aligning transport plans substantially outperforms a counterpart based on transport distance. The authors also report strong performance when calibration uses only node attributes, without edge information, and robust results under high perturbation rates. These findings support learning from detailed cross-graph correspondences: the matching pattern can provide a useful training signal beyond a single distance value or a binary pair label.
neurips-2023-galopa-graph-transport-lear.tldr: GALOPA learns graph representations by aligning input and representation-space transport plans, preserving detailed cross-graph matching information.

paragraphs: Differentiable environments make analytical gradients available for learning a policy, providing information about how changes in behavior affect outcomes. This paper integrates that information with Proximal Policy Optimization, or PPO. Its central concern is how to use these gradients while adjusting their influence when their estimates are unreliable.

The method introduces an α-policy, described as a locally superior policy, to bring analytical gradients into the PPO framework. Changing α controls how strongly those gradients affect learning. The authors also propose measures of gradient variance and bias, reducing reliance on analytical gradients when either measure indicates a problem. The local qualification matters: the construction does not assert that this policy is globally optimal.

Evaluations cover function optimization, physics simulations, and traffic control environments, with the proposed method outperforming baseline algorithms in the reported scenarios. The contribution is an adaptive connection between PPO and information available from differentiable environments. Its findings support modulating that extra information according to estimated reliability instead of assigning it an unchanging role throughout training.
neurips-2023-gradient-informed-proximal-.tldr: The method augments PPO with analytical environment gradients and adaptively reduces their influence when estimated bias or variance is high.

paragraphs: This paper explores whether the generalization abilities of text-guided image generation can help build agents that perform varied tasks. It reformulates sequential decision making as video generation: a textual goal specifies what should happen, and a planner produces future frames depicting a proposed course of action.

Control actions are then extracted from the generated video. This separates expressing a plan visually from translating it into actions. Text provides a way to describe novel combinations of goals, while images offer a shared representation for environments with different state and action spaces. The paper uses this formulation to support learning and generalization across robot manipulation tasks.

The approach also incorporates pretrained language embeddings and widely available internet videos to transfer knowledge into realistic video plans for real robots. Its central contribution is the policy-as-video formulation, which connects goal descriptions, visual prediction, and control. The claimed generalization rests on this common visual interface and compositional use of language; the paper's motivation toward broadly capable agents does not establish that every possible task can be solved.
neurips-2023-learning-universal-policies.tldr: The paper turns text-specified goals into video plans and extracts control actions, creating a shared visual formulation for varied robot tasks.

paragraphs: A shallow ReLU network can fit known observations while leaving open how it behaves between the regions those observations cover. This paper studies that interpolation behavior through minimum-norm interpolants: functions that fit the observations while minimizing a norm. The question is which fitting solution training and regularization favor.

The theoretical result concerns empirical risk minimizers trained with weight decay. As both the number of data points and network parameters tend to infinity, these minimizers converge to a minimum-norm interpolant if the regularization coefficient decreases at a precisely specified rate. The rate condition is essential to the claim; simply making weight decay small is not the stated guarantee.

The authors also numerically investigate common optimization algorithms, both with and without explicit regularization. They examine whether the algorithms themselves favor known minimum-norm interpolants, a phenomenon called implicit bias. Together, the analysis and numerical study distinguish a conditional convergence result produced by explicit regularization from empirical evidence about the preferences of optimization procedures.
neurips-2023-minimum-norm-interpolation-.tldr: Shallow ReLU risk minimizers converge to minimum-norm interpolants when weight decay vanishes at a precise rate as data and network size grow.

paragraphs: Some vision-and-language models accept sequences that mix images and text, allowing prompts to include demonstrations or questions connecting multiple images. Training for that interface requires similarly interleaved data. This paper addresses the lack of publicly available large-scale resources of that form by adding images to the text-only C4 corpus.

Multimodal C4 uses CLIP features and a linear assignment algorithm to position images within longer passages. The authors show that this placement process outperforms alternatives. The assignment step matters because the resource includes associations between images and particular surrounding text, supporting learning from documents that combine the two modalities.

After filtering content such as NSFW images and advertisements, the corpus contains 101.2 million documents, 571 million images, and 43 billion English tokens. Manual inspection of a random document sample finds 88% of images topically relevant and 80% aligned with specifically suitable sentences. These sample-based findings provide evidence about placement quality, while the released corpus supplies large-scale interleaved material across everyday subjects.
neurips-2023-multimodal-c4-an-open-billi.tldr: Multimodal C4 adds hundreds of millions of images to C4 documents using learned image-text features and an assignment algorithm.

paragraphs: Globally optimizing a decision tree can improve accuracy and produce smaller trees that people can more easily understand. General-purpose optimization solvers, however, face scaling difficulties. Dynamic programming can exploit the tree's structure by treating subtrees as independent subproblems, provided the optimization objective permits that decomposition.

This paper establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for that separability. The distinction is useful because decomposing a tree is only valid when solving its parts separately remains compatible with the overall objective. The authors use the characterization to generalize earlier dynamic programming approaches into a framework that handles any combination of separable objectives and constraints.

Experiments across five application domains demonstrate the framework's breadth and report substantially better scalability than general-purpose solvers. The result provides both a theoretical test for when subtree-based optimization applies and a practical framework for using it. Its scope is explicitly tied to separability: the contribution expands the supported objectives and constraints within that class, rather than claiming that every tree optimization problem decomposes.
neurips-2023-necessary-and-sufficient-co.tldr: The paper characterizes exactly when decision-tree objectives separate across subtrees and builds a scalable dynamic programming framework for that class.

paragraphs: Neural combinatorial optimization learns to construct solutions to difficult discrete problems, reducing dependence on specialized algorithm design. A major obstacle is scale: many constructive models struggle when problem instances become large. This paper focuses on learning from small instances while retaining the ability to solve much larger ones.

The proposed Light Encoder and Heavy Decoder, or LEHD, dynamically captures relationships among all currently available nodes across different instance sizes. This design supports adapting the solution-construction process to problems of varying scale. The authors complement the architecture with a data-efficient training scheme and a flexible mechanism for constructing solutions.

After training on small problems, LEHD produces nearly optimal solutions for the Travelling Salesman Problem and Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with up to 1,000 nodes. It also generalizes well to real-world instances from TSPLib and CVRPLib. These reported results improve the state of the art for constructive neural combinatorial optimization and support shifting modeling capacity toward decoding. The demonstrated near-optimality is an empirical finding, rather than an exact optimality guarantee.
neurips-2023-neural-combinatorial-optimi.tldr: LEHD uses a light encoder and heavy decoder to generalize from small training instances to routing problems with up to 1,000 nodes.

paragraphs: Off-policy evaluation estimates how a policy would perform using previously collected trajectories instead of new deployments. Human feedback makes this difficult because it can depend on multiple underlying factors and appear only sparsely. Methods designed around environmental rewards may therefore struggle to estimate policies' performance according to human feedback.

The proposed OPEHF framework reconstructs immediate human rewards so that existing evaluation methods can better use the available feedback. Reconstruction is regularized using environmental knowledge represented in a latent space. That representation captures both state-transition dynamics and the process associated with issuing feedback, tying the inferred reward signal to information about the environment.

The authors test the approach in two real-world experiments, adaptive in-vivo neurostimulation and intelligent tutoring, plus a visual question-answering simulation. They report significantly more accurate human-feedback estimation than directly applying existing off-policy evaluation methods or their variants. The findings support reconstruction as a way to make sparse feedback more useful for offline policy assessment, which matters when testing policies through fresh deployments is expensive.
neurips-2023-off-policy-evaluation-for-h.tldr: OPEHF reconstructs immediate human rewards using latent environmental knowledge to improve policy evaluation from sparse offline feedback.

paragraphs: Reducing numerical precision can make vision Transformers smaller and faster, but sub-8-bit values do not automatically produce faster execution. Commodity processors commonly offer SIMD instructions operating at eight bits or wider. PackQViT addresses both the model's sensitivity to quantization and the hardware challenge of executing low-precision operations efficiently.

Its quantization-aware training handles long-tailed activations with log2 quantization or clipping and regulates recurring channel-wise outliers in residual connections. Because those outliers have systematic patterns, their channels and regularized scales can be anticipated without runtime adaptive selection. Integer implementations of Softmax, LayerNorm, and GELU support an integer-only computation flow, while a packed 4-bit multiplier targets mobile acceleration.

On ImageNet, the authors report accuracy improvements over prior quantization work of 0.4%–17.9% at eight-bit precision and 0.4%–2.8% at four-bit precision. On a Realme GT phone with a Snapdragon 870 CPU, multiplier comparisons show speedups of 2.6–3.7 times and 3.8–5.9 times in the respective precision settings. These findings demonstrate benefits from coordinating quantization-aware modeling with concrete execution support.
neurips-2023-packqvit-faster-sub-8-bit-v.tldr: PackQViT combines activation-aware quantization training, integer operations, and packed multiplication to accelerate vision Transformers on mobile hardware.

paragraphs: Predictive models often need to capture interactions among several input features. Explicitly including polynomial terms of fixed orders can create a combinatorial explosion, while learned interaction orders may adapt poorly across different regions of the input space. This paper proposes varying the interaction structure locally through a Polyhedron Attention Module, or PAM.

PAM divides the input space into polyhedral regions and constructs a polynomial model within each region. The expressions defining the region's boundary hyperplanes are multiplied to form interaction terms. This makes the interaction order adaptive to the individual region. The resulting structure is also intended to identify which feature interactions matter for predicting the target.

Theoretical analysis establishes stronger expressive capability than ReLU-activated networks. Experiments report superior classification performance on large click-through-rate prediction datasets and meaningful interaction effects in a medical problem. These findings connect the architecture's mathematical construction to prediction and interpretation: different parts of the feature space can use different interaction orders, while exposing interactions relevant to the output.
neurips-2023-polyhedron-attention-module.tldr: PAM builds piecewise polynomial models whose feature-interaction orders adapt to different regions of the input space.

paragraphs: Restoring an image requires understanding the degradation affecting it as well as reconstructing useful content. This paper argues that models can gradually lose degradation information during learning when they do not explicitly use it for restoration. PromptRestorer preserves a dedicated path for that information to guide the recovery process.

The architecture has two branches: one restores the image, and the other perceives degradation-related information and prompts the restoration branch. A pretrained model extracts degradation features from observations. A perception modulator combines self-attention and pixel-wise modulation to process those features from both global and local perspectives, providing guidance at complementary spatial scales.

A gated propagation mechanism controls how the perceived information reaches the restoration branch, allowing it to adaptively learn useful features for recovery. Experiments report state-of-the-art results on deraining, deblurring, dehazing, and desnowing. The findings support treating degradation perception as an explicit component of image restoration. Here, prompting refers to learned degradation guidance within the architecture, rather than a requirement for written instructions from a user.
neurips-2023-promptrestorer-a-prompting-.tldr: PromptRestorer uses a dedicated degradation-perception branch to guide image recovery, reporting leading results across four restoration tasks.

paragraphs: Remote-sensing images contain valuable information, but assigning labels at the pixel level is difficult and expensive. This leaves substantial amounts of imagery unavailable for supervised segmentation training. The paper addresses that bottleneck by combining the Segment Anything Model with existing remote-sensing object-detection datasets to generate a much larger segmentation resource.

The resulting dataset, SAMRS, contains 105,090 images and 1,668,241 instances. It includes object categories, locations, and instance information, supporting semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and object detection separately or together. The authors describe its size as several orders of magnitude beyond existing high-resolution remote-sensing segmentation datasets and provide an analysis of its properties.

Preliminary experiments highlight the value of segmentation pretraining on SAMRS before fine-tuning. They suggest this can help address discrepancies between tasks and ease the constraint imposed by limited fine-tuning data. The contribution combines an efficient dataset-generation pipeline with a large training resource; the evidence about downstream pretraining benefits is explicitly preliminary, rather than a universal guarantee for every remote-sensing application.
neurips-2023-samrs-scaling-up-remote-sen.tldr: SAMRS uses Segment Anything and existing detection datasets to create large-scale remote-sensing segmentation data with promising preliminary pretraining benefits.

paragraphs: Federated learning must accommodate clients whose data and performance needs differ. A single shared model may not serve them all well, motivating personalized local models alongside a generic global model. This paper questions approaches that describe the relationship between those models primarily through similarities in their weights or divisions of their architectures.

The proposed spectral distillation method instead uses model spectrum information to capture representations that are related but distinct. A co-distillation framework then establishes a two-way connection between generic and personalized training. This allows the two training processes to inform one another while retaining the distinction between shared knowledge and client-specific representations.

The authors also introduce a wait-free local training protocol that uses time clients would otherwise spend idle in conventional personalized federated learning. Experiments across multiple datasets and heterogeneous data settings report improved performance and effectiveness for both spectral co-distillation and the training protocol. The paper therefore addresses two complementary issues: how shared and local models exchange knowledge, and how local training time can be used more effectively.
neurips-2023-spectral-co-distillation-fo.tldr: Spectral co-distillation links global and personalized federated models through spectrum information and uses otherwise idle time for local training.

paragraphs: Training can favor particular solutions even without an explicit penalty specifying which solution to choose. This implicit bias may help a network generalize, but the paper asks whether it also supports resistance to adversarial changes. It studies gradient flow in two-layer ReLU networks under a specific clustered-data setting.

The analysis assumes that correlations between cluster means are small. Within this setting, gradient flow favors solutions that generalize well and avoids harmful overfitting, even when the network has many more parameters than might be needed to fit the data. This establishes a benefit of the optimization dynamics despite the network's capacity to fit undesirable solutions.

The same dynamics nevertheless lead to vulnerability to small adversarial perturbations measured in the ℓ2 norm. Robust networks fitting the data do exist, so the vulnerability is associated with the solutions favored by training rather than their absence from the model class. The result separates ordinary generalization from adversarial robustness under the stated assumptions: successful prediction on new data does not ensure resistance to deliberately chosen small changes.
neurips-2023-the-double-edged-sword-of-i.tldr: For clustered data with weakly correlated means, gradient flow favors two-layer ReLU networks that generalize well but remain adversarially vulnerable.

paragraphs: Giving a model a geometrically structured latent space can support interpretation and generalization, but it also constrains how data can be represented. This paper investigates training difficulties caused by those topological constraints. Such difficulties concern the overall arrangement of the encoding, beyond whether individual points have locally reasonable representations.

The authors characterize obstructions theoretically and empirically. They show that local optima can arise from singularities, such as self-intersections, or from an incorrect degree or winding number. They then discuss how normalizing flows could potentially avoid these traps by defining multimodal variational distributions, allowing a data point to be represented through multiple modes over the geometric space.

Motivated by that possibility, the paper proposes a flow-based model that maps points to these multimodal distributions. Evaluations on two domains find more stable training and a higher chance of obtaining a homeomorphic encoder, which preserves topological structure. The evidence supports improved training behavior and likelihood of success, rather than a guarantee that the proposed model eliminates every topological obstruction.
neurips-2023-topological-obstructions-an.tldr: Multimodal flow-based encodings improve training stability and the chance of preserving topology when geometric latent spaces create optimization traps.

paragraphs: Graph-level anomaly detection identifies whole graphs that differ substantially from most examples in a collection. An abnormality score alone does not explain which parts of a graph drive the decision. This paper formulates explainable detection as predicting both the graph's abnormality and a subgraph that provides a rationale.

The proposed SIGNET model produces these two outputs together. Its design follows a multi-view subgraph information bottleneck framework, using the input graph and its dual hypergraph as complementary views. It assesses abnormality through mutual information across views and extracts bottleneck subgraphs in a self-supervised manner. Those selected subgraphs serve as the explanations associated with the predictions.

Experiments on 16 datasets demonstrate the model's anomaly-detection capability and self-interpretability. The approach matters because explanation generation is part of how the model represents and evaluates graphs, linking the prediction to selected graph structure. The findings support jointly learning detection and informative rationales, rather than treating the identification of an unusual graph as the entire task.
neurips-2023-towards-self-interpretable-.tldr: SIGNET jointly detects anomalous graphs and extracts explanatory subgraphs through a self-supervised multi-view information bottleneck.
